title: Transferring a design with a water-soluble pen
subtitle: Drawing directly onto fabric with a pen whose marks disappear in cold water.
excerpt: A water-soluble pen lets you draw or trace a design directly onto fabric. The marks rinse away in cold water once stitching is complete. Test on a scrap first: some fabrics stiffen slightly where the pen was used.
sourceNotes: Technique based on contemporary needlework practice. Water-soluble pens are a 20th-century development. Design transfer principles consistent with Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776.

glossaryTerms.definition: Fabric pen marks that dissolve in cold water. The pen's dye is water-soluble rather than permanent. Cold water removes the marks; heat (iron or tumble dryer) can set them permanently.

content.text: on fabric that disappear in a rinse of cold water. Drawing or tracing a design directly onto the cloth with the pen before stitching gives you clear guide lines to follow.

items.name: Design printed or drawn on paper

content.text: Test the pen on a scrap of the same fabric. Rinse the test swatch in cold water after marking and check the marks disappear completely and the fabric remains undamaged.
Place the design under the fabric and the fabric over a light box, or tape both to a window in good daylight so you can see the design through the cloth.
Trace the design lines onto the cloth with the water-soluble pen. Use light strokes; do not press hard.
Mount the fabric and stitch over the traced lines.
Once stitching is complete, rinse the piece in cold water. Do not use heat (no iron, no warm water) until all marks are gone.

items.symptom: The pen marks don't disappear after rinsing
items.cause: The marks were ironed before rinsing, or a heat-erasable pen was used by mistake.
items.fix: Soak in cool water for 20 minutes. If the marks persist, the iron may have set the dye permanently. Always rinse in cold water first, iron after.

items.symptom: The fabric stiffens where the pen marks were
items.cause: Some fabrics react to the pen's dye.
items.fix: Test on a scrap first. If stiffening occurs, use carbon paper or prick-and-pounce instead.

content.text: Water-soluble pen transfer is the fastest method for surface embroidery and crewelwork. It suits curved designs that are hard to position with carbon paper.
